clue.text: Imagine many in Rome are unhappily married

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, a large number

indicators.note: an unhappy state is a disturbed one, so the word beside it is thrown out of order

parts.note: M is the standard abbreviation for married

explanation.surface: Picture the many unhappy marriages of ancient Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Many' often stands for a large Roman numeral; here 'in Rome' confirms it is D.
explanation.definitionFit: To dream is to picture something in the mind, a verb close in sense to imagine.

clue.text: Problems if Formula One craze dies at the borders

indicators.note: the outside word sits at the edges, split so that its ends wrap round everything else

parts.note: taken as written, split D and IES around the rest
F for formula plus I, the Roman numeral one
a cult is a fashionable craze

explanation.surface: Motor racing is in trouble because enthusiasm for it is fading at the edges.
explanation.walkthrough: Formula One is a convention pair: F for formula, I for the Roman numeral one. The outer word is split across its interior rather than kept whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Difficulties are troubles or obstacles, a plural noun matching problems.

clue.text: Curious pride I harboured in EU's classical dramatist

indicators.note: something harboured is sheltered inside, so these letters go within the next word
curious means odd or strange, so the following letters take an odd new order

parts.note: taken as written, with the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: An odd national vanity sheltered within the European Union's drama tradition.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive S counts as a letter, so the rearranged letters sit between the U and that final S.
explanation.definitionFit: Euripides was one of the three great tragic playwrights of ancient Athens.

clue.text: Possibly lead me to think about law, initially

indicators.note: initially points at the opening letter of each word in the phrase it follows

parts.note: the first letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A lead in an argument might nudge me to reflect on the law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' reads as a verb guiding someone, but it is the heavy element; 'Possibly' marks it as one example among many.
explanation.definitionFit: Lead is one example of a metal, hence the hedging word in the definition.

clue.text: Intruding unsuccessfully to catch daughter with George

indicators.note: to catch something is to hold it, so the phrase before encloses the next letter

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
G is a standard abbreviation for George

explanation.surface: A man called George fails in his attempt to sneak in and grab a daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: IN VAIN takes D between VA and IN, then G follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Invading means entering by force where one is not welcome, a participle matching intruding.

clue.text: Anxious I will shortly meet a wind-up merchant

parts.note: a tease is someone who likes to wind people up

explanation.surface: Someone nervous about an encounter with a habitual joker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind-up merchant' is British slang for a person who enjoys provoking others with jokes.
explanation.definitionFit: To be ill at ease is to feel uncomfortable and nervous, an idiom matching anxious.

clue.text: Massive tax besets Sweden

indicators.note: to beset is to surround on all sides, so the first word goes round the second

parts.note: S is the international vehicle code for Sweden

explanation.surface: A huge tax burden hits the Swedes.
explanation.walkthrough: VAT, value added tax, is the British sales tax.
explanation.definitionFit: Vast means immense in size, a straightforward synonym of massive.

clue.text: Puts trust in son after department's closure

indicators.note: after places the word before it second, behind the pieces that follow in the clue

parts.note: DEP is an abbreviation for department

explanation.surface: A parent relies on a child once the office shuts down.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-S is possessive: the closure of the department, so the abbreviation is followed by a word for closure.
explanation.definitionFit: To depend on someone is to rely on them, a phrasal verb matching puts trust in.

clue.text: Half of hyenas have a large bone in the nose

indicators.note: half of a word keeps only one of its two equal portions

parts.note: the second three of its six letters
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Some hyenas have a big bone sticking out of the snout.
explanation.definitionFit: A nasal is the nasal bone, one of the pair forming the bridge of the nose.

clue.text: Top quality support should arrive the next day

parts.note: first-class means of the highest grade
a post is an upright support

explanation.surface: An excellent backing will turn up tomorrow.
explanation.walkthrough: First-class post is the faster tier of the British Royal Mail service.
explanation.definitionFit: First-class post in Britain is the mail service that aims to deliver by the next working day.

clue.text: Offended by strange dress fashion

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape or make, so these letters are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: Someone is shocked by a bizarre outfit in the latest style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' looks like the anagram signal, but it is fodder; 'fashion' at the end does the work.
explanation.definitionFit: To offend in the old sense is to sin or break a rule, which is what transgressed means.

clue.text: Discourteous? I am the complete opposite

parts.note: the exact opposite of the definition word

explanation.surface: A rude person is accused, and protests to be the very reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: The opposite meant is the opposite of 'Discourteous' itself, so I'M + POLITE.
explanation.definitionFit: Impolite means lacking good manners, a direct synonym of discourteous.

clue.text: Bone structure can be learnt

indicators.note: can be suggests the letters may become something else once rearranged

explanation.surface: Anatomy students are told the skeleton is something one can memorise.
explanation.definitionFit: An antler is a branched bony growth on a deer's head, so a structure of bone.

clue.text: Dishonest for a French worker to protect revolutionary communist

indicators.note: to protect is to surround and shield, so the outer letters go round the inner
a revolution turns things round, so the communist word is read backwards

parts.note: red is a common term for a communist; reversed
a hand is a manual worker

explanation.surface: A French labourer shields a communist rebel, which is deceitful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' looks like a description of the communist, but it signals turning the word round.
explanation.definitionFit: Underhand means secret and deceitful, an adjective matching dishonest.

clue.text: Horribly rude about the Yes vote — regret it happened

indicators.note: about means around, so the scrambled word wraps the following words
something done horribly is messed up, so the next word's letters are scrambled

parts.note: aye or ay is a yes vote in parliament

explanation.surface: Someone is bitter about a referendum's yes result.
explanation.walkthrough: Aye, often spelt ay, is how British MPs vote yes in the House of Commons.
explanation.definitionFit: To rue the day is an idiom for bitterly regretting that something ever occurred.

clue.text: Establish what belongs to me as supporter of the Queen after Edward retires

indicators.note: in a down entry a supporter sits underneath, so the word before this phrase goes at the bottom
after places the royal abbreviation behind the name that comes later in the clue
to retire is to go back, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: Ted is a pet name for Edward; reversed

explanation.surface: A royalist proclaims loyalty once Prince Edward steps down.
explanation.walkthrough: Ted is the usual short form of Edward; ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: To determine a fact is to establish or ascertain it, a verb matching establish.

clue.text: Urge knight on to scorn

parts.note: to spur is to urge on
N is the chess notation for knight, placed on the end

explanation.surface: Encouraging a knight to treat someone with contempt.
explanation.definitionFit: To spurn is to reject with disdain, a verb matching scorn.

clue.text: Worldwide Anglo-Dutch company sacks the French on half pay

indicators.note: to sack is to dismiss, so the following letters are thrown out of the company name

parts.note: le is French for the; removed

indicators.note: half keeps just one of two equal portions of a word

parts.note: the first half of salary, a word for pay

explanation.surface: A multinational lays off its French staff and halves wages.
explanation.walkthrough: Unilever is the Anglo-Dutch maker of soaps and foods; pay must first become salary before it can be halved.
explanation.definitionFit: Universal means applying everywhere, so worldwide is a close synonym.

clue.text: To some extent, appointment as teacher makes sense

indicators.note: to some extent means partly, so only a portion of the following words is used

explanation.surface: Getting a teaching job is fairly logical.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of appointment through as into the start of teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: Taste is one of the five senses, alongside sight, hearing, touch and smell.

clue.text: Offering a conclusion on the back of abridged text

indicators.note: abridged means shortened, so a letter is cut from the word

explanation.surface: A writer proposes a conclusion to follow a shortened manuscript.
explanation.walkthrough: Abridging usually trims the end, but here the word loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Extending means holding out or offering, as in extending an invitation.

clue.text: Crude oriental painting with heavy frame

parts.note: painting is a form of art

indicators.note: a frame is the edge of a picture, so only the outside letters are kept

explanation.surface: An unrefined Eastern picture in a chunky surround.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthy humour is coarse and down-to-earth, so crude is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Two rivers in the country

wordplay.note: R for river followed by the Ural, a Russian river

explanation.surface: A pair of rivers flowing through the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The country' looks like a nation, but as an adjective it means rustic.
explanation.definitionFit: Country as an adjective, as in country life, means rural rather than urban.

clue.text: Publicity by record company before first performance

parts.note: EMI is a British record label
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: A record label arranges promotion ahead of a show's opening.
explanation.definitionFit: A premiere is the opening public showing of a play or film.

clue.text: Child taken from mum in orphanage

indicators.note: taken from means extracted out of, so the letters are lifted from the words that follow

explanation.surface: A child is removed from its mother and placed in an orphanage.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor is a person under the age of legal adulthood, so a child.

clue.text: Island for a Cambridge graduate

parts.note: Bachelor of Arts, a first degree

explanation.surface: A holiday spot suitable for someone with a Cambridge degree.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuba is the largest island in the Caribbean.

clue.text: Organised workers crippled NATO industries

indicators.note: crippled means damaged and broken up, so the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Striking labour has crippled the alliance's defence manufacturers.
explanation.definitionFit: Trade unionists are members of labour unions, workers who are organised collectively.

clue.text: He joins in the fun to compete against another team

parts.note: to play a side is to compete against it

indicators.note: another version of a word is a different arrangement of the same letters

explanation.surface: A sporting fellow takes part for the pleasure of facing a rival side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another team' reads as a rival side; it means the letters of team rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A playmate is a companion in play, someone who shares the games and fun.

clue.text: Annoyed that every other part of train went in front

indicators.note: every other means taking alternate letters, skipping one each time

explanation.surface: A passenger is irritated that half the carriages went ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Riled means irritated or provoked, a past form matching annoyed.
